newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish investors' faith in EMU schedule up - poll.
newsitem.headline: Danish investors' faith in EMU schedule up - poll.

text.p: Close to half of decision makers at Denmark's leading institutional investors now believe that economic and monetary union will go ahead on January 1 1999, compared to five percent a year ago, a new poll shows.

A poll of 50 senior executives undertaken by unit trust Danske Invest showed that 48 percent believed that monetary union would take place as planned, 38 percent thought it would stick to the timetable but only a few members and 14 percent believed it would be postponed.

The comparitive figures for the same poll a year ago were five percent, 60 percent and 30 percent, with a further five percent believing that the project would be scrapped completely, a view held by none in the latest survey.
The poll was conducted between May 22 and May 29, before the French left's election victory and Sweden's announcement that it would not join EMU at the start date, although both were expected.
Denmark has already opted out of monetary union as a result of a binding 1993 referendum. A new plebiscite, for which there are no immediate plans, is required to reverse that decision.
